msg_album_completed_title.description: Tooltip on the star badge drawn over the cover of an album that has been played through to completion. Rendered fresh on every card; nothing is persisted under this text.

msg_album_cover_alt.description: Alt text for an album cover image when there is no album name available to use as its label. AD-8: the stored value is never rewritten, this is display only.

msg_album_hide_tracks.description: Label of the button on an album card while its track list is expanded. The opposite state reads as "View Tracks".

msg_album_played_songs_header.description: Heading above an album's track list when the full official tracklist is not known yet, so only the songs actually heard are listed. $1 is the number of distinct songs played.

msg_album_status_completed.description: Status pill of an album card that has been played to completion. $1 is the number of complete playthroughs. Keep the star and the "x" multiplier marker as written; both read the same in every language.

msg_album_status_completed_next.description: Status pill of a completed album that also shows how far the next playthrough has got. $1 complete playthroughs so far, $2 tracks matched so far in the next playthrough, $3 tracks on the album.

msg_album_status_played_songs.description: Status pill of an album with no known tracklist: just how many of its songs have been played. Do not confuse with msg_songs - this one carries the verb.

msg_album_status_played_songs_one.description: Singular form of msg_album_status_played_songs. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_album_status_played_songs_zero.description: Zero form of msg_album_status_played_songs. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_album_status_progress.description: Status pill of an album that is part-way through: how many of its songs have been heard. $1 songs heard, $2 songs on the album, $3 percentage complete.

msg_album_total_plays.description: Play total shown under an album name on its card. "Total" qualifies the count, so keep the word next to the number in a natural word order.

msg_album_total_plays_one.description: Singular form of msg_album_total_plays. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_album_total_plays_zero.description: Zero form of msg_album_total_plays. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_album_tracks_header.description: Heading above an album's track list once the full official tracklist has been resolved. $1 is the length of that tracklist.

msg_album_view_tracks.description: Label of the button on an album card while its track list is collapsed. The opposite state reads as "Hide Tracks".

msg_albums.description: Stand-alone count of albums. Used inside composed sentences where the noun has to agree with the number, so it must work as a phrase on its own.

msg_albums_one.description: Singular form of msg_albums. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_albums_zero.description: Zero form of msg_albums. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_artist_unknown.description: Stand-in for a missing artist name on the scanner's now-playing line. AD-8: "Unknown" is a persisted sentinel that also travels inside export bundles, so it is translated only where it is displayed and never on the way into storage.

msg_artists.description: Stand-alone count of artists. Used inside composed sentences where the noun has to agree with the number.

msg_artists_one.description: Singular form of msg_artists. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_artists_zero.description: Zero form of msg_artists. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_cache_clear_error.description: Inline error shown after the cover thumbnail cache could not be cleared. $1 is the underlying failure text from the cache layer.

msg_cache_cleared.description: Inline confirmation shown after the cover thumbnail cache has been emptied.

msg_cache_covers.description: Number of album covers held in the thumbnail cache.

msg_cache_covers_one.description: Singular form of msg_cache_covers. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_cache_covers_zero.description: Zero form of msg_cache_covers. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_cache_size_kb.description: Cover cache size in kilobytes. The divisor is binary (1024) and $1 is already rounded to one decimal place. Keep the unit attached to the number.

msg_cache_size_mb.description: Cover cache size in megabytes. The divisor is binary (1024x1024) and $1 is already rounded to two decimal places.

msg_cache_size_refreshed.description: Inline confirmation shown after the cover cache statistics were re-read on demand.

msg_count_hour.description: Hours component of the total listening time readout. Abbreviated to match the compact style of the existing readout. Shared with the popup duration display. Also used as a plural set: this key is the _other/_one form, with _zero alongside it.

msg_count_minute.description: Minutes component of the total listening time readout. Shared with the popup duration display. Also used as a plural set: this key is the _other/_one form, with _zero alongside it.

msg_count_play.description: Stand-alone count of plays, used inside composed sentences where the noun has to agree with the number. Owned by B2 and shared with the popup. In music software a play is one listening of a track - do not translate it as "track" or "stream".

msg_count_song.description: Stand-alone count of songs, used inside composed sentences where the noun has to agree with the number. Owned by B2 and shared with the popup. A song is a track as the listener hears it; keep it distinct from the play count.

msg_debug_boundary_date.description: Sync-boundary row of the debug panel for the legacy day-header boundary format. $1 is the date header from the history page; $2 is an already-pluralized play phrase such as "5 plays".

msg_debug_boundary_none.description: Sync-boundary row of the debug panel before the first sync has established one.

msg_debug_console_cleared.description: Contents of the debug log pane right after the Clear Logs button is pressed.

msg_debug_queueing.description: Transient label of the "Fetch Missing Tracklists" button while the backfill request is being queued.

msg_debug_storage.description: Storage summary row of the debug panel. All four arguments arrive already pluralized, in the order plays, songs, artists, albums (e.g. "1 play, 40 songs, 12 artists, 9 albums"). Keep the order and treat each as a finished phrase.

msg_debug_tab_connected.description: YouTube Music tab row of the debug panel after the content script answered a ping. $1 is the number of library items it reported.

msg_debug_tab_connected_one.description: Singular form of msg_debug_tab_connected. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_debug_tab_connected_zero.description: Zero form of msg_debug_tab_connected. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_debug_tab_none.description: YouTube Music tab row of the debug panel when no music.youtube.com tab is open.

msg_debug_tab_unreachable.description: YouTube Music tab row of the debug panel when a YouTube Music tab is open but its content script did not answer.

msg_debug_tracklists_all_resolved.description: Enrichment status tag after a manual tracklist backfill found nothing left to fetch.

msg_debug_tracklists_queued.description: Enrichment status tag after a manual tracklist backfill has been queued. $1 is the number of tracklists to resolve.

msg_debug_tracklists_queued_one.description: Singular form of msg_debug_tracklists_queued. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_debug_tracklists_queued_zero.description: Zero form of msg_debug_tracklists_queued. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_debug_watermark.description: Sync-boundary row of the debug panel for the current watermark format. $1 is an already-pluralized track phrase such as "200 tracks", $2 is the title of the newest entry. $2 comes from YouTube Music and is inserted as plain text.

msg_details_albums_show_all_count.description: Label of the Top 3 / Show All toggle while the top-three view is showing, as rendered from JS with the album count attached. $1 is the total number of tracked albums. The same span (#toggleAllAlbumsText) carries msg_details_albums_show_all_albums as its pre-render default in details.html; the JS value always wins once the list is rendered.

msg_details_albums_show_top3_only.description: Label of the Top 3 / Show All toggle while the full list is showing, as rendered from JS. Shared span with msg_details_albums_show_all_count.

msg_details_albums_subtext_showing_all.description: Sub-line under the Albums Breakdown heading while the full album list is open, as rendered from JS. $1 is the total number of tracked albums. The same node (#albumsSectionSubtext) carries msg_details_albums_subtext_default as its pre-render default in details.html.

msg_details_albums_subtext_showing_top3.message: Showing Top 3 most played albums ($1 total tracked).
msg_details_albums_subtext_showing_top3.description: Sub-line under the Albums Breakdown heading while only the three most-played albums are listed, as rendered from JS. $1 is the total number of tracked albums.

msg_enrich_step_done.message: Album metadata is up to date.
msg_enrich_step_done.description: Scanner-panel line for the album-metadata backfill once it has finished. This is not a history sync and must not be worded as one.

msg_enrich_step_scanning.description: Scanner-panel line while the album-metadata backfill is running. It shares the panel with the history sync but is a different task, so never word it as a sync.

msg_export_error.description: Toast shown when the export button failed unexpectedly, for example when the download could not be prepared. $1 is the raw error text from the browser.

msg_export_failed.description: Toast shown when the background refused to produce an export bundle. $1 is the reason it returned.

msg_export_success.description: Toast shown after a library export has been downloaded.

msg_generic_error.description: Stand-in for a value that could not be read, used by the cover cache statistics.

msg_import_error.description: Toast shown when an import failed for a reason with no dedicated message. $1 is the background's own English fallback text and will read as English.

n.example: Import payload must be a valid JSON object.

msg_import_error_bad_schema.message: Import failed: the backup is missing its songs or artists data.
msg_import_error_bad_schema.description: Import toast for a bundle that parsed as JSON but does not match the export schema.

msg_import_error_not_json.message: Import failed: the file is not a JSON object.
msg_import_error_not_json.description: Import toast for a payload that is not a JSON object at all.

msg_import_error_unrecognized_format.message: Import failed: this is not a recognised JAMt backup.
msg_import_error_unrecognized_format.description: Import toast for a JSON file that contains no songs, artists or albums, in other words somebody else's export.

msg_import_invalid_json.description: Toast shown when the chosen file could not be parsed as JSON at all, before it was ever sent to the background. $1 is the parser's own message.

n.example: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 412

msg_import_success.description: Toast shown after a successful library import. All three arguments arrive already pluralized, in the order songs, artists, albums (e.g. "40 songs, 12 artists, 9 albums"). Keep the order and treat each as a finished phrase.

msg_relative_days_ago.description: Elapsed time in whole days. Fallback used only on engines without Intl.RelativeTimeFormat; the normal path asks Intl instead.

msg_relative_days_ago_one.description: Singular form of msg_relative_days_ago. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_relative_days_ago_zero.description: Zero form of msg_relative_days_ago. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_relative_hours_ago.description: Elapsed time in whole hours. Fallback used only on engines without Intl.RelativeTimeFormat; the normal path asks Intl instead.

msg_relative_hours_ago_one.description: Singular form of msg_relative_hours_ago. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_relative_hours_ago_zero.description: Zero form of msg_relative_hours_ago. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_relative_just_now.description: Elapsed time for anything under a minute. Deliberately not a relative-time phrase: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat cannot produce this without making the number explicit.

msg_relative_minutes_ago.description: Elapsed time in whole minutes. Fallback used only on engines without Intl.RelativeTimeFormat; the normal path asks Intl instead.

msg_relative_minutes_ago_one.description: Singular form of msg_relative_minutes_ago. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_relative_minutes_ago_zero.description: Zero form of msg_relative_minutes_ago. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_relative_recently.description: Vague elapsed time used when no timestamp is recorded at all, for example the sync pill before the first sync. Deliberately vaguer than msg_relative_just_now.

msg_scan_error_scan_failed.message: The scan could not be completed.
msg_scan_error_scan_failed.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress error code "scanFailed": a history scan failed while importing the plays it had found. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_error_untrusted_source.message: The extension rejected the request as coming from an untrusted page.
msg_scan_error_untrusted_source.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress error code "untrustedSource": the extension refused a message because it did not come from its own page. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop. Users should never normally see this; it indicates a broken install or a tampered page.

msg_scan_reason_complete.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress reason "complete": the scan ran normally to the end, with nothing unusual to report. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_reason_end_of_history.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress reason "endOfHistory": the scanner scrolled back to the beginning of the listening history without finding the previous sync position, so there was nothing left to read. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_reason_full_history.message: Reached the 200-song history limit. Reopen the History page to sync further.
msg_scan_reason_full_history.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress reason "fullHistory": YouTube Music only exposes the most recent 200 history entries per page load, so the scan stopped after 200 entries. Two sentences; the second tells the user what to do next. Keep the number 200 as written unless your language has a different convention for expressing it. This replaces the old "reached 200-song limit" fragment that had to be stripped back out of a free-text status string, and is now a statement about the product rather than a parsing workaround. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage.

msg_scan_reason_navigated_away.message: The History page was closed before the sync finished.
msg_scan_reason_navigated_away.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress reason "navigatedAway": the user left the YouTube Music History page while the scan was still running, so it was stopped. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_reason_up_to_date.message: Nothing new since the last sync.
msg_scan_reason_up_to_date.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress reason "upToDate": a scan ran and the history contained nothing newer than the previous sync. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_step_boundary.message: Finding where the last sync stopped...
msg_scan_step_boundary.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress step "boundary": the scanner has loaded history entries and is matching them against the stored sync position so it can resume instead of re-reading everything. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis.

msg_scan_step_done.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress step "done" when no more specific reason accompanies it: the sync completed without anything further to explain. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_step_failed.message: The sync stopped with an error.
msg_scan_step_failed.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress step "failed". Prefer the matching msg_scan_error_* string when one applies; this is the generic fallback. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_scan_step_importing.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress step "importing": the harvested plays are being written into the library. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis.

msg_scan_step_progress.description: Scanner-panel line combining a step description with its progress. $1 is an already-localized step phrase such as "Importing your plays...", $2 is how many items have been processed and $3 how many there are in total. Treat $1 as a finished phrase. Keep the parentheses and the slash order intact.

msg_scan_step_saving.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress step "saving": the imported batch is being persisted. Names its object like its siblings ("Scanning your history...", "Importing your plays...") - do not shorten it to a bare "Saving...". Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage.

msg_scan_step_scanning.description: Scanner-panel line for the scanProgress step "scanning": walking the History page looking for plays. Composed at render time from a machine code, never written to storage. Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis.

msg_scanner_enrich_progress.description: Counts row of the scanner panel during an album-metadata backfill. $1 albums resolved so far, $2 in total.

msg_scanner_enrich_resolving.description: Counts row of the scanner panel during a backfill that has not yet worked out how many albums it will fetch.

msg_scanner_finding_songs.description: Scanner-panel line before a sync has identified its first track.

msg_scanner_in_progress.description: Label of the Start Sync button while a sync is running.

msg_scanner_interrupted.description: Scanner-panel line when a sync stopped reporting and there is no step left to describe.

msg_scanner_interrupted_hint.message: $1 Reopen the history page to resume.
msg_scanner_interrupted_hint.description: Scanner-panel line combining whatever the scan last reported with the advice to reopen the History page. $1 is an already-localized status phrase, so treat it as a finished phrase and keep the sentence boundary.

msg_scanner_live_counts.description: Counts row of the scanner panel during a live sync. $1 arrives already pluralized ("12 plays" / "1 play") and $2 is an already-pluralized song phrase ("40 songs" / "1 song"). Both are finished phrases - do not attach a noun to either, only arrange them.

msg_scanner_metadata_fetching.description: Badge on the scanner panel while album-metadata enrichment is running.

msg_scanner_metadata_ready.description: Badge on the scanner panel once album-metadata enrichment has finished.

msg_scanner_now_playing.description: Scanner-panel line naming the track a live sync has just read, for a track that carries no album. $1 is the title, $2 the artist. Both come from YouTube Music and are inserted as plain text, never as markup.

msg_scanner_now_playing_album.description: Scanner-panel line naming the track a live sync has just read, with the album appended. $1 title, $2 artist, $3 album. All three come from YouTube Music and are inserted as plain text, never as markup.

msg_scanner_plays_synced.description: Counts row of the scanner panel after a sync finished: how many plays that sync imported. Keep the past-tense sense.

msg_scanner_plays_synced_one.description: Singular form of msg_scanner_plays_synced. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_scanner_plays_synced_zero.description: Zero form of msg_scanner_plays_synced. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.

msg_scanner_start_sync.description: Label of the button that launches a history sync, in its idle state.

msg_settings_debug_tag_scanner_active.description: Scanner row of the debug panel while a history sync is running. $1 is an already-pluralized play phrase such as "12 plays" - treat it as a finished phrase.

msg_settings_scanner_badge_complete.description: Badge on the scanner panel after a sync that imported new plays.

msg_settings_scanner_badge_failed.description: Badge on the scanner panel after a sync that ended with an error.

msg_settings_scanner_badge_interrupted.description: Badge on the scanner panel when a scan stopped reporting - its tab was closed - so there is no verdict to show.

msg_settings_scanner_badge_up_to_date.description: Badge on the scanner panel after a sync that found nothing new to import.

msg_sync_status_ready.message: Sync Status: Ready for first sync
msg_sync_status_ready.description: Text of the history sync pill before any sync has run.

msg_sync_status_synced.description: Text of the history sync pill after a sync. $1 is an already-localized relative time such as "2 hours ago"; $2 is the title of the newest tracked song, which comes from YouTube Music and is inserted as plain text.

msg_tracks.description: Count of entries in the history-sync watermark. An entry is one row of the listening history, which may be a song, a podcast episode or anything else YouTube Music lists - keep the word as generic as the language allows.

msg_tracks_one.description: Singular form of msg_tracks. French uses this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_tracks_zero.description: Zero form of msg_tracks. Required because Brazilian Portuguese has a zero category, and shipped in every catalog so all six key sets stay identical.
